chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated to us, who said: al-Hasan ibn Ayyoob narrated to us, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from al-Ala' ibn Razeen, from Muhammad ibn Muslim ath-Thaqafi, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) that he heard him say:
Indeed, for the Qa'im (the Rising One) there are two occultations; in one of them it will be said to him: He has perished, and it is not known which valley he has followed.

key_terms.لِلْقَائِمِ: The Rising One (referring to the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of the Qa'im mentioned in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) outlines the two stages of the Qa'im's occultation, beginning with the 'Minor Occultation' characterized by widespread doubt and the claim that he has perished, as people were unaware of his specific path. This period of uncertainty served to test the faith of the companions before the transition to the Major Occultation, a concept central to Twelver Shia eschatology regarding the Mahdi's hidden presence.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (8) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah narrated from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Rabah from Ahmad bin Ali al-Himyari from al-Hasan bin Ayyoob from Abdul Kareem bin Amr from al-Ala’ bin Razeen from Muhammad bin Muslim ath-Thaqafi that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said:
“Al-Qa’im disappears twice. In one of them it will be said: He has perished or it is unknown which valley he has followed.”
